title: Wiki Viewer Architecture
subtitle: Measured map of one Next.js server, its browser clients, agent API, and local stores

structures.name: Web shell
structures.what: The browser workbench where people browse folders, open files, and review changes.
structures.how: App routes, layout, wiki shell, viewer toolbar, and shared UI compose the protected workbench.

children.name: App routes
children.what: Load the protected shell and route-level page surfaces.
children.how: Next.js pages in src/app compose the sign-in, share, and main workbench surfaces behind the middleware gate.

children.name: Wiki layout
children.what: Compose navigation, directory tree, tabs, and the main canvas.
children.how: layout.tsx plus the wiki sidebar and shell components assemble the directory tree, tabs, and viewer canvas into one protected frame.

children.name: Shared UI
children.what: Provide dialogs, menus, forms, and status primitives.
children.how: Reusable components in src/components/ui centralize dialogs, menus, forms, and status elements used across surfaces.

children.name: Viewer toolbar
children.what: Expose file actions, history, sharing, and view controls.
children.how: The editor toolbar and file actions menu wire view controls, history, sharing, and view-mode buttons to hooks and API calls.

structures.name: Editor and viewers
structures.what: Shows many file types and lets people edit Markdown with rich interactions.
structures.how: TipTap extensions and viewer components handle Markdown, documents, media, notebooks, and websites.

children.name: TipTap editor
children.what: Turns Markdown blocks into an editable document.
children.how: editor.tsx and extensions.ts register TipTap nodes and marks that map Markdown blocks to an editable ProseMirror document.

children.name: File viewers
children.what: Chooses a safe renderer for each supported file kind.
children.how: A viewer registry dispatches per-type renderers for images, PDFs, media, notebooks, CSVs, Mermaid, and websites.

structures.name: Page-shell hooks
structures.what: Connects page actions to workspaces, file trees, uploads, scratchpad, and navigation.
structures.how: Client hooks coordinate URL state, prefetching, workspace selection, and server calls.

children.name: File tree
children.what: Load directories and preserve expanded navigation state.
children.how: use-file-tree.ts fetches directory listings and keeps expanded nodes in sync with the active path.

children.name: Open file
children.what: Resolve selected files into editor or viewer content.
children.how: use-open-file.ts maps selected paths to editor content or the correct file viewer.

children.name: Workspace switcher
children.what: Change roots without losing the current page intent.
children.how: use-workspaces.ts lists roots and swaps the active workspace while preserving the current page.

children.name: Upload flow
children.what: Coordinate drops, progress, and post-upload refreshes.
children.how: use-upload.ts stages dropped files, tracks progress, and refreshes the tree after uploads land.

structures.name: Client state
structures.what: Keeps open pages, editor status, search, favorites, and agent activity responsive.
structures.how: Zustand stores combine page caching, autosave state, revision recovery, and browser preferences.

children.name: Page state
children.what: Track open paths, active tabs, and route transitions.
children.how: Zustand stores hold open paths, active tabs, and route transition state shared across the shell.

children.name: Editor state
children.what: Track dirty content, save status, and revision recovery.
children.how: editor-store.ts tracks dirty content, save status, and revision recovery for the active document.

children.name: Search state
children.what: Keep query, result scope, and selected matches stable.
children.how: search-store.ts keeps query, scope, and selected matches stable across navigation.

children.name: Activity state
children.what: Surface agent events, presence, and collaboration status.
children.how: ai-panel-store.ts and proof-store.ts hold agent events, presence, and collaboration status.

structures.name: Agent panel
structures.what: Lets people register agents, inspect activity, and follow collaboration status.
structures.how: A small client surface polls activity and calls registration, approval, and presence APIs.

structures.name: Middleware gate
structures.what: Stops protected pages before the app shell loads when no session cookie exists.
structures.how: src/middleware.ts applies the cookie gate, lite-mode deny list, and pass-through rules.

structures.name: Human access
structures.what: Authenticates people and checks whether state-changing browser requests are allowed.
structures.how: Better Auth, session checks, CSRF origin checks, admin rules, and embed-key checks share one boundary.

children.name: Better Auth
children.what: Create accounts, sessions, and sign-in responses.
children.how: The Better Auth server instance issues accounts, sessions, and sign-in responses from the database adapter.

children.name: Session boundary
children.what: Resolve the current person before protected handlers run.
children.how: Session checks resolve the current person before protected route handlers execute.

children.name: Origin checks
children.what: Reject cross-origin cookie mutations.
children.how: CSRF origin checks reject state-changing requests that lack the expected origin.

children.name: Admin policy
children.what: Gate system settings and privileged app controls.
children.how: Admin rules gate system settings and privileged controls behind a role check.

structures.name: Workspace registry
structures.what: Selects one of the server's registered roots for each request.
structures.how: workspaces.ts, config.ts, and workspace-context.ts resolve workspace headers, access, git roots, and remote mounts.

children.name: Root registry
children.what: Stores and lists named workspace roots.
children.how: config.ts and workspaces.ts store and list the named roots registered for the server.

children.name: Request context
children.what: Resolves workspace identity and access for each request.
children.how: workspace-context.ts resolves the active workspace and access policy for each request.

children.name: Git roots
children.what: Recognizes repository-backed workspaces and branches.
children.how: Git root detection recognizes repository-backed workspaces and exposes their branches.

children.name: Remote mounts
children.what: Connects registered roots to remote folder mounts.
children.how: Remote mount config connects registered roots to SSHFS-backed folder mounts.

structures.name: Path containment
structures.what: Keeps file operations inside the selected workspace.
structures.how: resolveWorkspacePath realpaths roots, rejects traversal and denied segments, and checks symlink-safe ancestors.

structures.name: Browser wiki API
structures.what: Serves folder listings, file content, search, history, uploads, and watches.
structures.how: 31 route handlers resolve user workspaces, validate origins, call domain libraries, and serialize responses.

children.name: File operations
children.what: List, read, write, move, upload, and delete workspace files.
children.how: Route handlers validate origins and call the filesystem library for list, read, write, move, upload, and delete.

children.name: Git views
children.what: Expose history, diffs, branches, and repository actions.
children.how: Git routes wrap the git integration to expose history, diffs, branches, and repository actions.

children.name: Search and links
children.what: Serve content search, backlinks, and slug lookups.
children.how: Search routes invoke the search engine for content matches, backlinks, and slug lookups.

children.name: Watch stream
children.what: Connect browser directories to file events.
children.how: Watch routes subscribe request scopes to the watcher pool for file events.

structures.name: Agent HTTP API
structures.what: Gives approved automation agents scoped file and collaboration operations.
structures.how: 22 route handlers enforce bearer identity, workspace scope, path globs, revision checks, and operation permissions.

children.name: Raw filesystem
children.what: Read, write, search, move, and delete arbitrary file bytes.
children.how: Raw filesystem routes enforce bearer identity, workspace scope, and path globs before byte-level operations.

children.name: Markdown collab
children.what: Read snapshots and apply revision-checked block operations.
children.how: Markdown routes read snapshots and apply revision-checked block operations through the proof core.

children.name: Events and activity
children.what: Stream document changes and provenance to agents.
children.how: Event routes stream document changes and provenance to approved agents.

children.name: Registration
children.what: Register agents and expose approved scopes.
children.how: Registration routes record agents and expose their approved operation scopes.

structures.name: CLI launcher
structures.what: Starts the packaged server and manages local service or remote-mount setup.
structures.how: bin/ parses options, applies environment precedence, starts the standalone server, and exposes service helpers.

structures.name: System config API
structures.what: Changes workspaces, users, administrators, pins, and local settings.
structures.how: 14 route handlers use session and origin checks before mutating persisted configuration.

structures.name: Shared documents
structures.what: Publishes read-only document links with optional unlock and expiry controls.
structures.how: Share routes and shared-docs modules create opaque grants, validate unlocks, and render sanitized content.

structures.name: MCP adapter
structures.what: Lets MCP clients use the agent contract through a separate npm package.
structures.how: packages/wiki-viewer-mcp defines 13 Zod-backed tools and a typed HTTP client with revision and scope errors.

structures.name: Node app runner
structures.what: Runs trusted node-app folders and proxies their local web surface.
structures.how: app-runner.ts manages child processes, readiness probes, ports, logs, and access-checked forwarding.

structures.name: Git integration
structures.what: Shows repository history and supports safe branch-oriented workspace actions.
structures.how: git.ts wraps the system binary, scans for leaked credentials, and backs history, diff, branch, and clone routes.

structures.name: SSHFS remotes
structures.what: Makes remote folders appear as workspaces through a local mount boundary.
structures.how: sshfs.ts and mount helpers manage remote lifecycle, reconnects, and mount hazards.

structures.name: Proof core
structures.what: Applies structured Markdown edits while preserving revisions, references, comments, and suggestions.
structures.how: ops-applier.ts parses blocks, checks base revisions, applies operations, writes atomically, and updates sidecar metadata.

children.name: Block operations
children.what: Apply insert, replace, delete, and annotation operations.
children.how: ops-applier.ts applies insert, replace, delete, and annotation operations against parsed blocks.

children.name: Reference map
children.what: Keeps stable block references across edits.
children.how: block-refs.ts keeps stable block references valid across edits.

children.name: Sidecar state
children.what: Stores revisions, activity, comments, and suggestions beside files.
children.how: sidecar.ts and activity.ts store revisions, activity, comments, and suggestions beside each file.

children.name: Event bus
children.what: Publishes document changes to watchers and agents.
children.how: event-bus.ts publishes document changes to watchers and agent subscribers.

structures.name: Locking and audit
structures.what: Prevents concurrent edits from silently overwriting one another.
structures.how: Mutexes, proper-lockfile, leases, collab state, idempotency, rate limits, and audit rows protect writes.

structures.name: Watch and SSE
structures.what: Notifies browser and agent clients when files change outside their current request.
structures.how: watcher-pool.ts uses chokidar subscriptions, ancestor merging, scope rebasing, deduplication, and heartbeats.

children.name: Chokidar pool
children.what: Share filesystem watchers across compatible scopes.
children.how: watcher-pool.ts shares chokidar watchers across compatible scopes.

children.name: Scope rebasing
children.what: Map ancestor events back to subscribed workspace paths.
children.how: Scope rebasing maps ancestor events back to subscribed workspace paths.

children.name: Deduplication
children.what: Collapse repeated changes into useful event payloads.
children.how: Deduplication collapses repeated changes into one useful event payload.

children.name: Heartbeats
children.what: Keep long-lived browser and agent streams alive.
children.how: Heartbeats keep long-lived browser and agent streams alive.

structures.name: Search engine
structures.what: Finds files and content without loading an entire workspace into memory.
structures.how: Ripgrep adapters stream bounded JSON results, retry advanced patterns, and verify backlinks through Markdown parsing.

children.name: Ripgrep adapter
children.what: Stream bounded file and content matches.
children.how: rg-search.ts and rg-snippet.ts stream bounded ripgrep matches as JSON.

children.name: File paths
children.what: Filter hidden, denied, and out-of-scope paths.
children.how: rg-path.ts filters hidden, denied, and out-of-scope paths before searching.

children.name: Backlinks
children.what: Parse Markdown references and return incoming links.
children.how: backlinks.ts parses Markdown references and returns incoming links.

children.name: Retry policy
children.what: Retry advanced queries when the fast path rejects them.
children.how: The retry policy reruns advanced queries when the fast path rejects them.

structures.name: Markdown pipeline
structures.what: Converts Markdown into safe HTML and understands links, embeds, tasks, and frontmatter.
structures.how: Unified remark and rehype plugins parse, sanitize, rewrite relative assets, detect embeds, and cache output.

children.name: Parser
children.what: Build an AST from Markdown and GitHub-flavored syntax.
children.how: Unified remark plugins parse Markdown and GitHub-flavored syntax into an AST.

children.name: HTML renderer
children.what: Convert parsed content into safe display HTML.
children.how: to-html.ts runs rehype plugins and the sanitize schema to emit safe HTML.

children.name: Wiki links
children.what: Resolve internal links and relative asset references.
children.how: wikilink.ts resolves internal links and relative asset references.

children.name: Embeds
children.what: Detect supported external media and document embeds.
children.how: lib/embeds detects supported external media and document embeds.

structures.name: Scratchpad
structures.what: Captures quick snippets before they become normal workspace files.
structures.how: Scratch config and detection modules create, sweep, and promote temporary captures.

structures.name: Proof test suite
structures.what: Exercises the filesystem, auth, collaboration, and agent safety contracts.
structures.how: 71 proof test files run through scripts/test-floor.mjs, which enforces a 691-test minimum.

structures.name: Build and publish
structures.what: Checks changes and prepares the standalone package for release.
structures.how: Versioned workflows run formatting, tests, builds, and npm publishing around the one server artifact.

structures.name: Auth store
structures.what: Durable users, sessions, and account records.
structures.how: Better Auth uses a local SQLite store through the project database adapter.

structures.name: Share store
structures.what: Durable public-share grants, expiry data, and view counts.
structures.how: shared-docs/db.ts persists opaque share metadata in SQLite.

structures.name: Audit store
structures.what: Append-only records of scoped agent filesystem operations.
structures.how: proof/audit.ts writes operation, path, revision, and hash metadata to SQLite.

overview.what: Wiki Viewer is one local-first web server for browsing and editing many file types. Its browser workbench, scoped agent API, and MCP adapter all meet at workspace-aware filesystem operations, with Markdown collaboration adding revisions and provenance around ordinary files.
overview.how: The standalone Next.js server owns request routing, auth, workspace selection, path containment, rendering, git and remote adapters, app launching, and three SQLite-backed roles. Human saves and agent block operations share locks and revision checks. Chokidar watchers, SSE streams, and timers provide asynchronous behavior inside the same deployed service; no separate queue or worker service is present.
